evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips the time-boxed ask and dependable quote framing entirely. Opens with 'Let me check it for you' and moves directly into probing without the 10-15 minute frame or wait for yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after significant probing. Rep asks 'Do you have any special instructions or concerns about this move that you want us to discuss on this call as well?' — but only after already gathering addresses, floor counts, and item details.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'No, not in particular like I expected to be relatively straightforward move' — raises no concerns, so n/a applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised by customer, n/a applies.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides both a typical range and personalization: 'typically one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours to complete but this is more of just, you know, grand to ground, short distance... I just put your move Josh more on the four and a half to five and a half hour mark. So if the guy would be able to finish everything within four and a half hours it's $918. If it goes up to five and a half hours it's $1,122.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep delivers fee transparency upfront: '$102 per hour, per mover... that already includes the two men and the truck, all the robs. To protect your furniture... taxes, insurance, credit card fees, all of that is already in the price.' Also frames: 'two and a half hour minimum. Once we go over that minimum, we only charge in fifteen minute intervals.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' After delivering the estimate range ($918–$1,122), customer responds 'Yup, sounds good' but rep was not the one to solicit this reaction with the specific phrase and silence-hold.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'and lastly on time guarantee if we run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts for your move.' — full statement of discount-if-late, no ambiguity on terms.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep states: 'are no worries, damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement, for any accidental damages' — covers amount and purpose, but does not explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Instead moves directly to booking logistics: 'Alright, now if it's okay, I'll just adjust a little bit under the time of your schedule...'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asks a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or throwaway 'Any questions?' before closing. Moves directly to address confirmation.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Moves directly to 'I'll go ahead and send everything in an email' with no explicit ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: No mention of rate lock or deposit policy.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms: apartment numbers (1508 and 2309), moving date (Friday October 2nd), arrival window (adjusted to 12 noon–2 PM), and promises email. Missing: phone number, crew size confirmation, and crew notes about customer concerns.

top_strength: Joanna executed a thorough and well-structured logistics discovery—she gathered all key details on property type, floors, distances, parking, walking routes, and item inventory, systematically and professionally.
coaching_note: Joanna skipped the entire opening frame (quid pro quo), never asked for the business explicitly at the end, and missed the final concerns check and catch-all—three critical closing sections that leave real close risk and deal confidence on the table.
